source_text: Qui Adam forma dicitur futuri, id est Christi, verum forma a contrario, ut, sicut ille peccati, ita hic iustitiae forma credatur; sed sicut incarnatio Christi iustitiae fuit forma, non prima, sed maxima, quia et, antequam Verbum caro fieret, ex ea fide, quae in Deum erat, et in Prophetis et in multis aliis sanctis fulsere virtutes, veniente autem temporum plenitudine exacta in Christo iustitiae norma resplenduit et, qui praedictus fuerat pater futuri saeculi, tam praecedentium sanctorum quam etiam sequentium remunerator eminuit.
pass_a_gloss: Which Adam is said a form of the one to come, that is of Christ, but a form from the contrary, so that, as that one of sin, so this one may be believed a form of justice; but as the incarnation of Christ was a form of justice, not the first, but the greatest, because even before the Word became flesh, from that faith which was toward God, virtues shone both in the Prophets and in many other holy ones, but with the fullness of times coming an exacted norm of justice shone out in Christ and he who had been predicted a father of the age to come stood out as a remunerator both of preceding holy ones and also of those following.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin

pass_b_english: Adam is called a figure of the one to come, that is, Christ (Romans 5:14), but a figure by contrast: as the former is understood as a model of sin, so the latter is a model of righteousness. Yet Christ’s incarnation was not the first model of righteousness but the greatest. Even before the Word became flesh, virtues shone in the prophets and many other holy people through their faith in God (John 1:14). When the fullness of time arrived, however, the exact standard of righteousness shone out in Christ (Galatians 4:4). The one foretold as ‘Father of the age to come’ stood forth as the rewarder both of the saints who preceded him and of those who followed (Isaiah 9:6).

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

variants.reading: “Father of the age to come” preserves the Latin form of Isaiah 9:6 invoked by Julian, rather than replacing it with the common English “Everlasting Father.”
